transcript.content: Hello, please have a seat. What brings you into the clinic today?

Hi, thanks. Um, what finally made me come in is that I keep turning in applications or my research notes with these small, but really embarrassing mistakes. Like, I'll realize I mislabeled an artwork date, or I completely skipped a question on a form. And the frustrating part is that I honestly thought I had checked them over before handing them in. It's just happening enough that I figured I should talk to someone about it.
Roughly when did you first start noticing these kinds of mistakes happening?
I'd say it's been noticeable since I moved to Boston. That was right after I finished my bachelor's degree. So, um, counting back, it's been going on for about a year and 11 months now.
Looking back before the age of 12, did you ever struggle with focus, daydreaming, or making careless mistakes in school?

Yeah, I did. Even back in elementary school, my teachers would always write notes saying I had good ideas, but... I'd forget to actually turn in my worksheets. Or I'd lose the instructions and miss little details on assignments. 

It was a pretty regular thing. Honestly, the only way things got done was because my parents checked my backpack every single night to make sure I wasn't missing anything.

{"intent": "Assess for hyperactivity or impulsivity to differentiate between ADHD subtypes or criteria fulfillment.", "question": "Have you ever struggled with feeling restless, having trouble sitting still, or

No, not really. Um, I've never had much trouble sitting still. I'm usually pretty calm physically. I don't really get that restless feeling or feel like I need to be moving around all the time. It's really just my mind that wanders, not so much my body.
Do these difficulties with focus or staying organized also impact your daily personal life, like managing chores, bills, or appointments?

Yeah, they definitely do. I’ll mean to do normal adult things, um, like return an email, pay a bill, or pick up groceries... and then days later I realize I never actually did it. It's like it just completely drops out of my mind.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient presents with prominent symptoms of inattention, including frequent careless mistakes, difficulty sustaining attention to details, and forgetfulness in daily activities (e.g., bills, emails). Symptoms have been present since childhood (prior to age 12) and result in functional impairment across academic/work and personal domains. Hyperactivity and impulsivity symptoms are explicitly denied, supporting a diagnosis of attention deficit disorder without hyperactivity (ICD-10: F98.8).
